title: Project plan for Project Northcell: lifecycle model, work breakdown, schedule, gates, resources and progress

standards_mappings.rationale: Project management: project plan, schedule, resources, milestones and progress reporting.
The engineering phases this plan schedules.
Safety project management is a subset of this plan; the safety-specific activities themselves are in FB2-MAN-SPL-000001.

lifecycle_status_note: Set to the value above because no human has reviewed or approved this record. `automated_review_status` below refers to corpus automation (schema, link, provenance and consistency checks run by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py) and is not a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation.

revision_history.author: project_manager
revision_history.description: Project plan authored because MAN.3 was recorded as a coverage gap: the management domain held a project scope statement and change records, and neither is a plan. A scope statement declares a boundary; this record carries the schedule, the gates, the resource assignment and the actual-against-planned progress reporting that MAN.3 expects.

plan_basis: Derived from the work the corpus' existing records imply: a hazard analysis and safety goal that exist, four functional safety requirements with four hardware and three software requirements beneath them, a system-level chain that had no system requirements until this authoring pass, and no post-development work at all. The plan is sized for the gap between that state and a coherent lifecycle, not for a greenfield programme.
calendar_note: Every date in this record is synthetic. They describe the hypothetical Project Northcell as its own artefact says that programme does not exist. No date here is a real commitment, a real gate date or a real review date.

work_breakdown.work_package: Concept phase: item definition, hazard analysis, safety goal, functional safety concept
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Three domain experts part-time over one quarter plus a concept-review pass. An estimate, not a bottom-up derivation.

work_breakdown.work_package: Functional safety requirements and technical safety concept
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Follows the concept. Four requirements plus the technical concept.

work_breakdown.work_package: Stakeholder elicitation, use cases and system requirements
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: The largest single package. Eighteen records across two levels, and the elicitation that a real programme would have to do with people.

work_breakdown.work_package: Hardware and software requirements and detailed design
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Seven technical requirements. The corpus already held these; the estimate covers the re-baselining against the system requirements, not their first authoring.

work_breakdown.work_package: Verification planning and execution across concept, system, hardware and software
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Nine measures, none of which this corpus could execute; the estimate assumes the harnesses exist, which they do not.

work_breakdown.work_package: Supporting process definition and instantiation: quality, configuration, problem resolution, change control, supplier monitoring, reuse
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Definition plus one recorded instance each. A real programme would need far more instances; one is the minimum that distinguishes a process record from a policy.

work_breakdown.work_package: Post-development lifecycle: release identification, production and end-of-line test, calibration, field monitoring, service, decommissioning
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Six lifecycle areas, each documented to the level at which the corpus can state what it does not know.

work_breakdown.work_package: Measurement, risk management and process improvement
work_breakdown.estimate_basis: Continuous rather than a package; the estimate covers the setup pass and the first improvement cycle.

progress_records.narrative: Two weeks behind on the hazard analysis. The cause is not technical: the safety manager who was to review the severity and controllability reasoning was unavailable for eleven days and there is no second person qualified to do it. The plan named a single point of failure and the risk register's RSK-002 predicted exactly this.

Supporting process definition is the package actually behind. It was given 20 days of float and has consumed 55. The float was real: the package had no predecessor and was therefore expected to finish early. The variance is absorbed, not recovered, and this is stated rather than hidden in a re-baselined date.

Still behind after the reviewer returned. Recorded as behind rather than complete because the functional safety concept was baselined with two unresolved contradictions against the safety goal's timing budget, and a concept cannot be baselined while its own arithmetic does not close.

Stakeholder needs and system requirements on plan. The package recovered because WBS-006 finished late and released the system engineer, which is the opposite of what the float was for. Recorded because it is the kind of dependency that a plan which treats packages independently would miss.

Verification is the package driving the forecast. Not because the measures are hard to write but because none of the nine new measures can be executed: there is no security harness, no injection node and no vehicle. The plan assumed the harnesses would be built by the verification package and it does not fund them. This is a planning omission and the risk register's RSK-004 names it.

limitations: Synthetic. This plan schedules a hypothetical programme. No organisation, person, supplier or vehicle named here exists.

The effort estimates are order-of-magnitude figures produced by the author, not bottom-up estimates from a team that exists. They are recorded so that the schedule has denominators, not because they mean anything.
The progress records are authored, not collected. There is no project to report on, so these are synthetic observations with the same shape a real report would have.

The competence records this plan's resource table refers to do not exist. Naming a competence record that is absent is how a competence-management gap hides, so the resource table says 'not created' rather than leaving the field blank.
Four of the six gates carry an explicit note that the corpus does not currently meet their exit criteria. A plan whose gates all pass is a plan whose gates mean nothing.

The schedule does not account for the fact that the corpus's largest engineering gap was the absence of the work this plan schedules. It assumes the plan starts from a state in which concept-level work is partly done, which it is.
